lexSnapshot.derivativeNote: خَٰلِدُونَ is in the derivative form: خَالِدٌ
lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
خ/ل/د   kh–l–d mountains, rocks
; to remain put for a long time, to be forever, to be eternal, eternity, to grow old without showing physical signs of old age; to be well contented, to like someone or some place; to wear some kind of trinkets; mind; heart; spirit; a mole‐like animal.

Of this root, 7 forms occur 87 times in the Qur’an:
تَخْلُدُون takhludūn 2 times; أَخْلَدَ ʾakhlada 2 times; خُلْدٌ khuld 6 times; خَالِدٌ khālid 4 times; خَالِدُون khālidūn 70 times; خُلُودٌ khulūd 1 time; and مُخَلَّدُون mukhalladūn 2 times.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
خَالِدٌ khālid [act. part., pl. خَالِدُون khālidūn]

1 immortal

(7:20) وَقَالَ مَا نَهَاكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَذِهِ الشَّجَرَةِ إِلاَّ أَنْ تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ الْخَالِدِينَ he said, ‘Your Lord only forbade you this tree lest you become angels or of the immortals’

2 one living or remaining forever or for a long time

(9:100) وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي تَحْتَهَا الأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا He prepared for them Gardens through which streams flow, in which they abide forever

3 to live, to remain, to endure for a certain period of time without interruption

(11:107) خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ السَّمَوَاتُ وَالأَرْضُ there remaining in it for as long as the heavens and earth endure.

entries.label: أَخْلَدَ
entries.definitionHtml:
أَخْلَدَ ʾakhlada [v. IV]

1 [intrans. with prep. إلى] to incline to, to take to, to cling to, to give oneself completely to

(7:176) وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لَرَفَعْنَاهُ بِهَا وَلَكِنَّهُ أَخْلَدَ إِلَى الأَرْضِ وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ and had We willed, We could have raised him up by their means, but he clung to the earth and followed his desire

2 [trans.] to cause to be immortal, to cause to remain or live forever

(104:3) يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ thinking his wealth will make him live forever.

entries.label: تَخْلُدُ
entries.definitionHtml:
تَخْلُدُ takhlud [imperf. of v. خَلَدَ khalada, intrans.] to remain, last, endure for a long time or forever, to gain immortality

(26:129) وَتَتَّخِذُونَ مَصَانِعَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَخْلُدُونَ and do you build fortresses, so that you may remain forever?

entries.label: خُلُودٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
خُلُودٌ khulūd [n./v. n.] immortality, eternity, remaining for ever

(50:34) ادْخُلُوهَا بِسَلاَمٍ ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ الْخُلُودِ enter it in peace–this is the Day of Eternity.

entries.label: خُلْدٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
خُلْدٌ khuld [v. n./n.] immortality

(21:34) وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ الْخُلْدَ We have not granted to a human before you [Prophet] everlasting life.

entries.label: مُخَلَّدُون
entries.definitionHtml:
مُخَلَّدُون mukhalladūn [pl. of pass. part. مُخَلَّدٌ mukhallad] interpreted either as beautifully attired or as forever youthful

(76:19) وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدَانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ إِذَا رَأَيْتَهُمْ حَسِبْتَهُمْ لُؤْلُؤًا مَنْثُورًا [the] eternally youthful [lit. eternal youths] (or, beautifully attired youths) will attend them–if you could see them, you would think they were scattered pearls.
